Verified end to end: braceMatching (services.ts:2630-2635) maps only GreaterThanToken<->LessThanToken; getBraceMatchingAtPosition uses getTouchingToken and findChildOfKind, both of which walk `n.getChildren(sourceFile)` (utilities.ts:1580, 1144) i.e. createChildren. Post-change a JSX closing tag's leading token is a single LessThanSlashToken, so `braceMatching.get()` misses from the `<` side and `findChildOfKind(JsxClosingElement, LessThanToken)` misses from the `>` side — go-to-matching-brace returns emptyArray in both directions where it previously matched. Real editor-feature regression, distinct from the primary.

Refuted: a bare LessThanToken can never parent a JsxClosingElement, so the OLD check at utilities.ts:1892 did not match `< /div>` either — there is no regression. parseJsxChildren (parser.ts:6160-6179) drives parseJsxChild on scanner.reScanJsxToken(); a LessThanToken recurses into parseJsxElementOrSelfClosingElementOrFragment (parser.ts:6154), and the loop only breaks — reaching parseJsxClosingElement (parser.ts:6337-6339, which parseExpects LessThanSlashToken) — on LessThanSlashToken, ConflictMarkerTrivia, or EOF (parser.ts:6146). So `< /div>` yields a malformed opening/self-closing element, never a JsxClosingElement with a bare `<` child.

The reset at services.ts:530 is indeed load-bearing (the scanner is the module singleton exported at utilities.ts:391), but the finding asks only for an explanatory comment and reasons from a speculative future deletion. Taste-level maintainability nit; c3 is the substantive version of the same observation.
